jobs.occupation: Student Assistant for Software Development at Novo Nordisk Engineering
jobs.description:
Student Assistant for Software Development at Novo Nordisk Engineering

If you're energised by software development and thrive on solving real business challenges through technology, we'd love to hear from you!

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

We are looking for a student software developer to join our system development team in Global IT.

As a team, we support NNE's engineering project portfolios and build modern applications that help colleagues work smarter across projects and locations.

As a student software developer, you will play an important role in supporting the team's development efforts by contributing to real business-critical solutions, helping maintain high quality through testing, and bringing fresh perspectives on emerging technologies such as Azure and AI.

This is a part-time position of around 2–3 days a week. You will work on real tasks from day one, with a dedicated colleague to guide you, review your code and help you grow.

How you might spend your days

As a student software developer, you’ll be:

• Developing new features and fixing bugs in our applications, APIs and services

• Building front-end components and backend endpoints under guidance from experienced developers

• Helping perform testing of our applications, running test cases, reporting defects and writing automated tests to keep our quality high

• Taking part in our agile ways of working, stand-ups, sprint planning and code reviews

• Exploring new tools and technologies, such as cloud services on Microsoft Azure and AI and sharing what you learn with the team

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• A self-learner who picks up new technologies and tools on your own initiative and is not afraid to ask questions when you get stuck

• Structured and responsible, taking ownership of your tasks and delivering what you commit to

• Collaborative and comfortable working with colleagues across disciplines, locations and cultures

• Curious and proactive in suggesting improvements to tools, processes and technical solutions

• Open to feedback and ready to learn from mistakes, with high spirits and a sense of humour

What you bring to the role

In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• Are studying for a bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, software engineering or a related field

• Have a basic understanding of programming in C#/.NET or Python

• Have some experience with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and ideally a modern framework such as React

• Know the basics of relational databases and SQL

• Have used Git for version control

• Communicate well in English, written and spoken

It’s a bonus if you have tried automated testing, CI/CD or cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure.

Life at NNE

NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, NNE means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

You can read more about the benefits we offer here.

Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

Deadline of application is 15 November 2026

Questions before applying? Send us a quick text to arrange a convenient time to chat. Contact Manager Ivanna Jurkiv Ditlevsen at +45 3077 4721.

Please note:

• We only accept applications submitted through our online recruitment system

• You do not need to attach a cover letter, but please include a few sentences about why you are applying in your resume or CV

• We invite to interviews on a running basis.

Fair hiring:

At NNE, we are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunities for all job applicants. To maintain fairness, we request that you refrain from including a personal photo in your CV.

jobs.occupation: (Senior) Product Creation Learning Partner – Maternity Cover (Minimum 12 Months)
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about building change management and learning capabilities and fostering a learning culture at scale? Do you thrive when working with tools and processes, and are you naturally curious about finding new ways to use them? If so, you could be our Senior Product Creation Learning Partner during a maternity cover of at least 12 months.

At 3Shape, Product Creation is our term for R&D. It represents the organization responsible for developing and improving our products across hardware, software, engineering, and related product-development disciplines.

We are looking for an experienced learning partner to join us on a fixed-term maternity cover. In this role, you will build and embed a scalable capability framework that ensures Product Creation teams are equipped to work effectively across processes, tools, and ways of working.

During the maternity-cover period, you will use your stakeholder-engagement skills and your ability to align and influence across organizational levels and functions. You will combine these strengths with solid experience in building and maintaining training frameworks and structures that fit the organization’s needs.

You will be part of the Product Creation Excellence (PCE) team, which consists of around 10 people, all based in Denmark. Together, we enable Product Creation and adjacent functions across processes, training, tools, strategy, and transformation.

Core Responsibilities

Training framework & architecture

• Define the learning and capability framework and structures that support tool and process adoption, ways of working, and competence building: Standardize how training is designed, deployed, and maintained (including anchoring structures, super-user and ambassador methodologies, communities of practice, learning journeys, etc.).

• Continuously improve and expand the learning and capability framework and plan for Product Creation in collaboration with the Product Creation team.

• Develop and anchor training: Enable and support the organization to own and deliver training locally where appropriate, while ensuring central support and training structures are available where needed.

Capability mapping and training roll-out

• Continuously map and prioritize training needs with stakeholders based on business needs, maturity across technical functions, necessity, and criticality.

• Define and drive rollout plans in collaboration with functional owners and/or the PCE team.

• Establish regular cadences for training areas and structures, ensuring an appropriate frequency of training events, reviews of training materials, trainer setup and coaching, and cycles for communities of practice and other learning environments.

Integration with business & transformation

• Ensure alignment with transformation initiatives and operating model changes.

• Support change management and the adoption of new practices.

Capability tracking & improvement

• Define and follow up on KPIs for capability building (e.g., adoption, proficiency, and coverage).

• Drive feedback loops and the continuous improvement of the training setup.

• Maintain an overview of capability gaps and critical skill needs.

This role may involve some travel.

Ideal profile:

For this role, we believe a good fit is someone who can bring:

• Experience in building learning frameworks in complex medical regulated R&D or technology organizations (including experience with different training and learning models, e.g., train-the-trainer, communities of practice, coaching, and online training).

• A collaborative, team-oriented mindset. We depend on strong teamwork within the PCE team and across other teams and functions, so it is essential that you thrive when working with others to solve challenges and realize opportunities.

• An understanding of and/or interest in how different profiles learn, with the ability to balance technical tool training with soft skills such as leadership.

• Experience with change management and the large-scale rollout and/or adoption of new processes, preferably in a large R&D or other technical environment.

• Strong presentation and communication skills, with the ability to build bridges between technical and non-technical functions.

• The ability to drive adoption without formal authority.

Join us in shaping a company culture that makes Monday mornings worth it.

At 3Shape, you will join an international R&D environment in central Copenhagen, working closely with advanced hardware, software, and engineering teams that develop products to improve dental care globally. You will have the opportunity to shape learning and capability-building practices and see your work make a direct difference for colleagues.

We are a vibrant, visionary, and international place to work. But most of all, we are a diverse group of over 50 different nationalities who all contribute to a thriving company culture. We partake in social clubs, monthly social activities, and various in-team activities as well. If that’s not enough, then add on:

• Central Copenhagen location.

• A globally recognized technology company.

• An attractive healthcare package to keep you fit and well.

• Breakfast every day and a delicious, healthy lunch prepared by our private chefs.

• A joint purpose: to enable dentists to provide superior dental care to every patient, every time.

Apply Now

Join us for a maternity cover of at least 12 months and be part of a team improving treatment and care in a meaningful industry. We encourage all qualified professionals who are passionate about building strong learning capabilities in a complex product-development environment to apply.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis; however, we plan to conduct interviews in October and November.

We encourage all relevant applicants to apply. We are committed to celebrating human diversity, and we trust that the best way to reach outstanding business results, is by welcoming diverse people into our community.

jobs.occupation: Application Specialist, TMS Sea, Air & Logistics
jobs.description:
Do you have experience within Sea & Air Freight and an interest in IT, systems and process improvements?

At Blue Water Shipping, we are implementing CargoWise across our global organization and working towards more common processes across countries and business units.

To support this work, we are looking for an Application Specialist to join our TMS Sea, Air & Logistics (SEAL) team.  In this role, you will help ensure that our transport management system supports daily business needs and efficient ways of working across the organization.

About the role

You will become part of the SEAL Product Team within Digital Products, Global IT, working in an agile DevOps setup. The team is responsible for developing, maintaining and improving solutions that support our global Sea & Air business. As an Application Specialist, you will work closely with freight forwarding specialists, key users and colleagues in IT. Your focus will be to support and develop our transport management solutions to meet business needs and ensure stable operations. This role offers a chance to influence both processes and systems in a global organization working to standardize and improve processes across countries and business units.

Your key responsibilities

• Provide 2nd level support and maintenance of Blue Water's Sea & Air transport management solutions.

• Support the ongoing global CargoWise implementation and optimization initiative.

• Configure, test and deploy new functionality and system enhancements within CargoWise, including workflows, documents and reports.

• Work with users and business representatives to understand requirements and translate them into system solutions and product improvements.

• Support the testing, implementation and rollout of new CargoWise releases.

• Help ensure adoption of new functionality and ways of working across the business.

• Develop and maintain system documentation, user guides and knowledge articles.

• Support training activities and share knowledge with key users and colleagues.

• Participate in sprint planning, prioritization and ongoing improvements of our solutions.

• Follow up on solution performance and support continuous improvements together with users and key stakeholders.

About you

You have a background within Sea & Air freight forwarding and a genuine interest in systems, digital tools and process improvements.

Ideally, you bring:

• Experience from Sea & Air Freight Forwarding, preferably combined with Super User, System Administrator or project responsibilities.

• Experience with transport management systems, particularly CargoWise.

• CargoWise certification is considered an advantage.

• Knowledge of industry processes within international freight forwarding and logistics.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with users, business representatives and IT colleagues.

• A structured and analytical approach with the ability to work systematically with processes, systems and business needs.

• Experience working in agile environments or a willingness to learn.

• An interest in AI, automation and digital technologies, and how they can contribute to improving business processes and ways of working.

At Blue Water Shipping, we believe great results are created by people who enjoy their work and have the opportunity to grow. We offer an informal working environment where collaboration, trust and professional development are important parts of everyday life.

When joining us, you can expect:

• The opportunity to influence the global implementation and development of CargoWise.

• Professional and personal development in an international organization.

• A high level of responsibility and influence.

• Close collaboration across business and IT.

• Flexible working conditions and a supportive team environment.

• The opportunity to contribute to digitalization and continuous improvement initiatives within a global logistics organization.

• A workplace guided by Blue Water's core values, where strong results are achieved through teamwork, collaboration and a genuine Passion for People.

Location & Application

🏡 Flexible working conditions: We offer flexibility and the possibility to combine office and remote work.

📞 Questions about the position: For more information, feel free to contact Helle S. Christensen, Senior Manager, on +45 24984614.

At Siteimprove, we are the leader in agentic content intelligence. Siteimprove.ai is a unified platform that brings together accessibility, analytics, SEO/AEO, and content strategy into a single, continuous flow. Our AI agents work alongside marketing and digital teams — not instead of them — helping to create high-performing, accessible content that's easy to discover by both humans and AI.

As Senior Engineering Manager for Content Platform, you own the systems that acquire and ingest the content our entire product line reasons about. Our enterprise customers bring thousands of sites each, re-crawled continuously. Every accessibility finding, analytics number, and SEO recommendation begins as content one of your systems fetched, parsed, and stored.

You will lead two Copenhagen engineering teams, each with its own Technical Leader role held by a Principal Engineer. The two carry different hard problems. One sustains crawl throughput so that cost tracks value rather than volume. The other builds the shared foundations the rest of Siteimprove works through, so product lines reach content through common contracts rather than each solving it their own way. You represent this group's engineering in a trio with Product and UX. Pillar strategy is set with Seattle, nine hours behind you, and you are the leader on the ground who turns it into local decisions rather than waiting on it.

Your teams set the ceiling on what the rest of Siteimprove can build. Your goals follow from that — ingestion reliable enough that customers trust it, efficient enough that cost tracks value rather than volume, capable enough to feed our agentic products, and ready for the compliance bar our public sector customers require. You will use AI to build the platform that powers our AI products and stay close enough to the code to argue a design on its merits.

What we will be doing

• Decision Authority in Copenhagen: You are the decision-maker on the ground. Resolve in Copenhagen hours what would otherwise wait overnight. As engineering's voice in the group's trio, bring the constraints Product and UX have no way to see into scope conversations early enough to change them. Your director sets goals with you and discusses how you and the group are tracking against them.

• Platform Ownership: Own Content Platform's ingestion surface as a running business — availability, throughput, cost, and delivery predictability. Modernization is how you improve those numbers, not a separate program you report on. Our move to EKS is part of it. You decide which debt gets paid down and when and keep that trade-off in front of the trio.

• Architectural Direction: Own the constraints and the cross-team contracts your Technical Leaders design within: scheduling the crawl workload so cost tracks value rather than volume, moving ingestion onto event-driven services, and defining how the rest of Siteimprove consumes what we ingest. You will hold that direction with your senior engineers, because authority here is earned in design review.

• Delivery Under Pressure: Hold the delivery line when priorities move. Work arrives from outside the team continuously, and you will sequence so committed work reaches completion rather than stalling half-built. Align directly with peer engineering leaders and close the gaps at functions you depend on but don't manage.

• Measurable Impact: Define the KPIs these systems are judged by and hold your teams to them. You will prove the impact of what you prioritize in throughput, cost, and reliability rather than asserting it, and you will stop work that moves none of them.

• Growing Your Engineers: Own performance, career development, and compensation decisions for the group. Hand the Tech Vision and System Design for major initiatives to the engineers closest to the systems, and review rather than drive them.

• AI-Native Delivery: Use AI for engineering throughput, not just for product features. You will model the practice yourself: interpreting legacy code paths nobody documented, generating test coverage around behavior before you change it, and shortening the distance between a design decision and a working replacement

• Travel may be required; a valid passport is required

• Perform other duties as assigned

What we will require of you

• Ownership at Distance: A group whose outcomes you owned while the people setting direction sat elsewhere. We want evidence of decisions you made rather than escalated, because waiting would have cost more than being wrong. This role also asks for a standing weekly overlap in your late afternoon, when the Seattle day begins, so that the conversation with your director is a working one.

• Systems Depth: 7+ years in backend engineering, with real depth in distributed systems, high-throughput data ingestion, or crawling at scale. Comfort establishing how an undocumented system behaves before changing it, and the instinct to reach for AI to do that quickly.

• Leadership Through Leaders: 10+ years managing engineers, including senior technical leaders whose designs you reviewed rather than produced, and whose scope you expanded rather than absorbed.

• Architectural Judgment: A track record of moving established services onto cloud-native infrastructure and of designing interfaces other teams build on. What matters is having lived with both long enough to know which decisions held and which leaked.

Work Environment

• This is a hybrid role based in our Copenhagen office, with the opportunity to work from both the office and home. Our working language is English.

• Travel may be required up to 5% of the time.

• You will work across a nine-hour spread with product and engineering leadership in Seattle, and with peer teams in other Siteimprove locations. Your late afternoon overlaps the start of the Seattle day, and the role expects you to keep a weekly window there for goal-setting and progress discussions with leadership.

What we will love about you

These systems quietly carry the entire product. If you're ready to make them faster and cheaper to run without stopping the business that depends on them, we'd love to hear from you. Join us in helping enterprise marketing teams turn their vast content into clear, actionable insights that drive measurable business results.

What you'll love about us

We’re building the next generation of AI-powered content intelligence, helping organizations unify accessibility, SEO/AEO, analytics, and content performance into one platform. If you’re energized by solving complex problems, working cross-functionally, and contributing to a product with real-world impact, we’d love to connect.

In addition, we hope you will appreciate:

At Siteimprove, we're committed to supporting your wellbeing both at work and beyond. Our Denmark benefits are designed to help you thrive personally and professionally.

Rest and relaxation: Generous time off including Danish holiday entitlements, five additional FF Days, child sick leave, and bereavement leave.

Comprehensive benefits: Health insurance, company-paid mobile phone support, and internet allowance to support your day-to-day needs.

Prepare for the future: Danica pension with employer contributions to help support your retirement goals.

Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

**The Opportunity

**We are looking for a Full-Stack Software Engineer to join our Product Engineering organization and help build the digital experiences that teams, coaches, and athletes rely on every week.

In this role, you will work across the full stack—developing scalable backend services, designing resilient APIs, and building responsive, intuitive web interfaces. You’ll be part of a cross-functional product team partnering closely with Product Managers, Product Designers, native mobile engineers, and platform specialists to take ideas from concept to production.

Your work directly influences user engagement, product adoption, and long-term platform value. Whether it involves streamlining how users access and interact with our tools or helping them unlock deeper insights from their matchday media, you will build software that turns video and match data into meaningful, everyday habits for sports communities worldwide.

**What You Will Do

**

• Build and maintain full-stack capabilities, developing scalable backend APIs and high-quality web interfaces.

• Participate in the complete product lifecycle: from initial problem discovery, ideation, feature scoping, technical planning, design discussions, implementation, testing, deployment, and ongoing iteration based on user data.

• Partner with our native iOS and Android engineers to ensure backend systems and API contracts seamlessly support mobile-first user flows.

• Design clean data models, reliable integrations, and maintainable services with an eye toward performance and scale.

• Incorporate modern AI development tools into your workflow to iterate quickly and build thoughtful software solutions.

• Contribute to technical discussions, code reviews, and shared ownership of the team’s systems.

**What You Could Bring

**

• 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, ideally in a product-led environment.

• Experience working across frontend and backend development.

• A product mindset, with an interest in understanding real user problems and working with Product and Design to turn them into thoughtful technical solutions.

• Backend experience using Python, Rust, or another comparable language, together with relational databases such as PostgreSQL.

• Frontend experience using TypeScript or JavaScript and a modern SPA framework such as React, Vue, or Angular.

• Experience building reliable RESTful or GraphQL APIs for web or native mobile applications.

• A thoughtful approach to automated testing, CI/CD, and maintaining production-quality systems.

• Curiosity about modern AI development tools and how they can support everyday engineering workflows

jobs.occupation: Senior Director, Global Support Functions IT
jobs.description:
**THE OPPORTUNITY

**VELUX is the world's most recognised brand in roof windows and skylights, with a genuine mission: creating better living environments through daylight and fresh air. Backed by a foundation with a long-term ownership philosophy, this is a company that thinks in decades, not quarters.

IT in VELUX is entering a new chapter. A new strategy is taking shape, it is high on the Group agenda, and it comes with a clear long-term view of where we are going. At its heart is, of course AI and all the new tech, but even more so, are the platforms that run the business: SAP and Workday, supporting Finance, Sales, Operations, Supply Chain, and People & Organisation.

With a strong foundation already in place, we’re now looking for a leader to take it to the next level - evolving from classic ERP toward AI-enabled ways of working. For a leader who enjoys transformation, wants to shape a roadmap rather than simply run one, and gets energy from solving real problems, this role is worth a conversation.

**What You Will Lead

**You will be accountable for the strategy, delivery, and operation of the enterprise platforms behind VELUX global support functions and be a leader of leaders.

As part of a newly established IT leadership team, reporting to the CIO, you will contribute to the strategic IT agenda beyond your own area. You will own the budget, the key vendor relationships, and the portfolio of programmes across the support functions.

**What The Role Actually Involves

****Stabilising the core and delivering upgrades

**You’ll lead our work on platform reliability: setting up a clear roadmap, solving problems at their source, and keeping stakeholders informed and supported along the way.

**Rethinking the support model

**You’ll have the opportunity to reshape our SAP and Workday support model, building on what works today, including our partnership with an external provider, and shaping how it evolves.

**Prioritising with the business

**The transformation has strong backing, and a big part of the role is making sure effort goes where it creates the most value. With an established PMO behind you, you’ll strengthen portfolio governance and build alignment on priorities.

**Leading the AI shift

**AI is changing everything, including traditional systems. You will help define what AI-enabled ways of working mean for our applications and for our organisation. It is new ground for everyone, and mindset matters as much as technology.

**Who We Are Looking For

**You’re a hands-on IT leader who thinks strategically but isn’t afraid to get into the details. When something breaks, you look past the quick fix to find the real cause, bring the right people together, and make sure it gets properly resolved. People trust you because you deliver on what you promise.

You work in a lean, practical way, and when setting priorities, you involve people rather than handing down a list. You help stakeholders reach a shared view of what matters most, while keeping the conversation focused and constructive.

We are particularly interested in candidates who bring:

• 10+ years of IT leadership, including leading global, multi-disciplinary organisations.

• Experience with enterprise SAP landscapes across Finance, Sales, and Operations/Supply Chain; S/4HANA experience is a strong advantage.

• Experience with HR technology platforms, ideally Workday is an advantage.

• A track record of leading large upgrades and multi-year transformations in a global, matrixed organisation.

• Strong vendor management, including contracts with global system integrators and managed-service providers.

• Curiosity about AI and automation, and a practical view on how they can change the way we work.

• Experience from a manufacturing company is a distinct advantage, and from the building materials industry is a plus.

**Ready to apply?

**Learn more about the VELUX Group online at www.velux.com where you can read more about working at our company and what to expect of our recruitment process.

We look forward to receiving your application and CV as soon as possible. We are conducting interviews on an ongoing basis until we have the right match.

All inquiries will be treated confidentially.

**About VELUX

Bring your banking and data experience into our newly established Markets Data Office. Join us and work with critical data in Markets as part of a team that is being built right now. Join us in building a new data capability in Markets

About the job

At Saxo, we are building the Markets Data Office as part of our Data Governance Programme. The team is organised across four domain areas: Products, Operations, Counterparty Risk and Market Risk. Together, these areas reflect how critical data is used across Markets.

We are a newly established team and still in our build phase. Our first permanent colleagues joined in September 2026. Today, we are eight people, and we are growing to twelve.

As the team grows, we are creating the foundations for how we work, including frameworks, standards, tooling and governance practices. At the same time, we are already delivering on ongoing data initiatives across Markets.

This is an opportunity to join early, influence how we work and make a real impact on how data is governed at scale.

What you will do

As a Data Portfolio Analyst, you will take ownership of data governance activities within one of our four domain areas. You will work closely with business stakeholders, data owners, data stewards and technology teams to improve how critical data is defined, monitored and controlled.

Depending on your domain, you could work with instrument reference data, market data, price data, custody information, election data, trades, positions, counterparty risk or model data.

You will be part of one Markets Data Office with shared standards, tooling and governance practices, while also helping to define and improve these as the team develops.

Your responsibilities will include

• Taking ownership of ongoing data governance activities within your domain and driving them forward

• Identifying and documenting Critical Data Attributes (CDAs) by reviewing data attributes with stakeholders, assessing which are critical for Saxo and driving the governance of Critical Data Elements (CDEs)

• Analysing data together with data owners to assess quality, identify issues and lead root cause investigations

• Defining and maintaining data definitions, rules, thresholds and documentation used in monitoring and control activities

• Monitoring data quality outputs, tracking remediation and escalating when issues are not being resolved

• Building strong working relationships with data owners, data stewards and stakeholders across business and technology

• Helping shape the frameworks, standards and ways of working for the Markets Data Office

A key part of your role will be making sure documentation is clear, structured and easy to maintain, helping create transparency and consistency across the organisation.

Who you are

You bring:

• Some years of experience from the banking sector, which is a requirement for this position

• Experience in data analysis, data quality, data governance or a related field

• The ability to understand data in the context of business processes and explain your findings clearly to both business and technical audiences

• The ability to produce clear and structured documentation

• Hands on experience with SQL. Experience with Python is an advantage

• Experience using AI and other technology tools to automate tasks and find smarter ways of working

It would be a clear advantage if you have

• Experience from Markets functions such as trading, market or counterparty risk, investment products or operations, including an understanding of how a trade moves from front to back

• Experience with data governance in financial services, for example CDEs, data ownership, data profiling, data controls, data lineage or BCBS 239

• Experience with Databricks, Great Expectations, OpenMetadata or similar data platforms and data quality tools

We are looking for someone who:

• Takes ownership. You move your work forward, follow through and take initiative.

• Collaborates naturally. You build trust with business stakeholders, technology teams and colleagues across different domain areas.

• Uses technology naturally. You use technology to analyse, automate, document and find more effective ways of working.

• Is comfortable working in an evolving environment. You can manage changing priorities, bring structure to areas that are still developing and help shape solutions as the team grows.

• Is structured and curious. You have a strong analytical mindset, pay attention to detail and enjoy understanding how things work.

What we offer

• The opportunity to help build a new data function and its foundations from the ground up

• Real ownership and influence on how critical data is governed across Markets

• Exposure to key business domains and critical data flows

• The opportunity to work closely with experienced colleagues across Markets, data and technology

• A role that can develop alongside a growing team

You will join the Markets Data Office at an early stage of its journey, giving you the opportunity to take on new challenges, grow your responsibility and influence how critical data is managed across Markets.

We get curious people invested in the world

When you work at Saxo, you become a Saxonian and part of a purpose-driven organisation, where good ideas are always taken seriously, and where you can make a true impact. We are invested in your development, and you can expect a robust career from day one when you join Saxo – no matter which role you take on.

You will join 2,500 other ambitious colleagues across 11 countries and become part of an international organisation. Working in Saxo, you will get to meet colleagues from many different cultures and backgrounds, and you should know that we value diversity and inclusion and see it as a genuine source of strength to drive growth, foster innovation and position us for long-term success.

We encourage an open feedback culture and supportive team environments enabling employees to grow and fulfil their career aspirations.

When you bring passion, curiosity, drive and team spirit, your learning journey will be dynamic and your career opportunities in Saxo will be immense.

At Saxo we don’t just offer a job – we offer an opportunity to invest in your future!
